data.name: Bhaveta
data.gender_notes: Bhaveta is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Bhavetas are named after Bhava, the Sanskrit word for emotion. In Hindu mythology, Bhava is a manifestation of Lord Shiva, representing passion and love. Bhavetas are believed to embody these powerful emotions. The name Bhaveta carries the meaning “Lord of emotions” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Bhaveta usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of emotions and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Carriers of deep emotion and passion
data.etymology: Bhaveta belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of emotions.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Bhaveta total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

historical_references.reference: Bhaveta was a famous king of the lunar dynasty (Sourasenaka) who ruled in the early 5th century BCE. He is mentioned in various Jain texts and is known for his patronage of Jain monks and building several temples.

Bhavetas are mentioned in the Mahabharata as descendants of the lunar dynasty. One of them, Bhaveta, is a king who ruled during the Mahabharata war (around mid-4th century BCE). He was a powerful ally of the Pandavas and played a significant role in the war.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Bhaveta' is of Indian origin, derived from the Sanskrit word 'bhava' which means 'to be' or 'existence'. In Hindu mythology, Bhaveta is a rare name for a male deity often depicted as a manifestation of Lord Vishnu. However, in modern contexts, the name 'Bhaveta' is increasingly being used as a personal name in various communities, both in India and abroad. This name is particularly popular among those interested in Indian spirituality and mythology.
